comparison: Perfect claim overlap (C6, C89-C101) on expression mapping and network analysis. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with caveats about detection limitations for two receptors. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting 'limitations in what can be interpreted from single cell transcriptomic data' and describing findings as 'foundations for future studies' rather than definitive conclusions. This represents a meaningful disagreement in confidence level.

Perfect claim overlap (C108, C109, C111) on RFamide receptor findings. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes reliance on phylogenetic inference, while peer reviewers endorse this as part of the broader phylogenetic analysis demonstrating 'independent expansion' with 'compelling evidence.'

Perfect claim overlap (C112, C113) on PRGamide receptor orthology. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval distinguishes between direct evidence (orthology) and prediction (inference about other ancient peptides). Peer reviewers endorse this as demonstrating 'peptide-receptor coevolution' with 'compelling evidence.'

Perfect claim overlap (C114, C115) on utility of neuropeptide expression as cell-type markers. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this requires experimental validation. Peer reviewers treat this as a logical extension, acknowledging it 'provides foundations for extensive functional characterization.'

Perfect claim overlap (C116) on overall deorphanization success. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval quantifies ~42% success rate. Peer reviewers describe this as 'the most extensive pharmacological characterization of neuropeptide GPCRs in a cnidarian to date' and 'a huge step forward.'

High claim overlap (85% Jaccard) on pharmacological screen results (C60-C76). OpenEval includes C4, C5, C59 not in peer result. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes EC50 values and statistical rigor. Peer reviewers describe this as 'the most extensive pharmacological characterization' using 'established and widely used methodologies' providing 'compelling evidence.'

Good claim overlap (64% Jaccard) on peptide library creation (C3, C44, C46-C48, C50, C51). OpenEval includes C45, C49 not in peer result; peer includes C4, C5 not in OpenEval R1. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes mass spectrometry validation and identification of 15 new precursors. Peer reviewers endorse the 'established and widely used methodologies' providing 'compelling evidence.'

Moderate claim overlap (48% Jaccard) on phylogenetic findings (C77-C86). Peer R3 also includes evolutionary conclusions (C7, C8, C42, C87, C88, C102-C104, C106, C107) not in OpenEval R4. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on ancestral families and expansion patterns. Peer reviewers explicitly endorse the conclusion of 'independent expansion' providing 'fundamental new insights.'

Moderate claim overlap (43% Jaccard) on evolutionary conclusions (C7, C8, C87, C88, C102-C104, C106, C107). Peer R3 also includes phylogenetic claims (C42, C56, C77-C86) not in OpenEval R5. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes reliance on phylogenetic inference and potential for incomplete sampling. Peer reviewers strongly endorse this as demonstrating 'independent expansion' and providing 'fundamental new insights into the evolution of neuropeptide signaling systems.'

Minimal claim overlap (only C56) on GPCR diversity analysis. OpenEval R3 focuses on C52-C58 (GPCR diversity, HMMer searches, CLANS clustering). Peer R3 addresses broader evolutionary conclusions. Both rate as SUPPORTED where they overlap, but address largely different aspects of the phylogenetic analysis.
